title: Bunny Bell and the Wobbly Seven
markdown:
Once upon a time, in a town full of tinkling bells and giggling gardens, lived a bunny named Bunny Bell. Bunny Bell was quite possibly the fluffiest bunny you ever did see, with ears that practically did a little dance when she was excited. She was very often excited, especially about shiny things! Her burrow was a treasure trove, a cozy, underground nest overflowing with pebbles that sparkled like tiny stars, dewdrops she'd carefully captured in hollowed-out acorn cups, and even a lost button that gleamed like a pearl. Her heart would thump-thump-thump a little too fast whenever she spotted something new and wonderfully shiny.

Every day was a happy routine for Bunny Bell, a symphony of soft hops and delighted sighs. She’d wake up with the sunbeams tickling her nose, then hop out of her burrow and spend her morning polishing her collection, arranging them just so on mossy shelves and smooth stones. She’d hum little tunes that sounded like bubbling brooks and dream of what glorious, sparkly treasure she might find next. She was ever so good at finding things, her keen eyes spotting glints from afar, but oh, she was a little impatient! If a shiny thing was just out of reach, her whiskers would droop for a second, before she'd try to grab it with a frantic wiggle and a hopeful wriggle of her nose.

Until one day, a most unusual thing happened! The Grand Town Clock, the one with the giant, booming chimes, let out a particularly loud “BONG!” And with that bong, something slipped! Down, down, down it tumbled, a single, shining number, a perfect, golden Seven, straight into the sparkling, gurgling fountain in the very center of the town square. It was the number Seven. A big, bright, brassy Seven, catching the sunlight and winking like a playful eye.

“OH NOOOO!” squeaked Bunny Bell, who had been enjoying a particularly juicy clover bloom nearby, her ears flopping right down in dismay. “The Grand Town Clock just coughed up a number! A shiny, golden Seven! And it’s gone *plink* into the fountain!” The Seven! It was so wonderfully shiny! It was so perfectly round and solid! And it was right in the middle of the fountain, bobbing gently on the surface of the water, just out of her reach. She tried to stretch her little paws, reaching and reaching. She even tried to hop onto a slippery, moss-covered stone at the very edge of the fountain. *WHOOSH!* Her back feet slid on the damp moss, and she tumbled onto the soft grass with a gentle, fluffy *poof*. She wiggled her nose sadly. This was a problem, a very shiny, very bobbing problem indeed.

Bunny Bell decided she absolutely needed some help. And who better to help than Cog the brass squirrel? Cog lived in the grand old oak tree by the library, and he was known far and wide for being as clever as he was shiny. He was made entirely of gleaming brass, every bit of him polished to a warm glow, with tiny gears that whirred softly inside him when he was thinking hard. Bunny Bell scampered over, her fluff bouncing with urgency. “Cog! Cog!” she panted. “The Grand Town Clock dropped a Seven! It’s in the fountain, and I can’t get it! It’s just too… watery!”

Cog’s little brass ear twitched. He scurried down the rough bark of the oak tree, his tiny metal feet making a delicate *tick-tock* sound. He peered at the fountain, his polished glass marble eyes focusing. Indeed, there it was, the beautiful Seven, glinting in the water like a captured sunbeam. Cog tried to reach it with his own paws, extending his arm as far as it would go. *Clink!* His brass fingers just brushed the cool surface of the water. He couldn't quite get it. He tapped his brass chin thoughtfully, a series of soft clicks. This was proving to be trickier than finding a lost acorn.

Cog’s whirring mind started to work overtime. He remembered something he’d read in one of the old science books from the library, a book with pages as thin as butterfly wings. Something about how water isn't quite like air. He remembered reading that when light travels from the air into the water, it slows down, and that makes things look bent, or shifted. Like a straw in a glass of water looks all wiggly and out of place! Cog’s eyes widened with understanding. “Aha!” he chirped, his internal gears spinning a little faster, making a happy little whizzing sound. “Bell! I have an idea! It’s a bit… wobbly, but I think it will work!”

Cog explained his clever plan, his voice a series of soft, metallic chirps and clicks. “See, Bell,” he said, pointing a shiny, slender finger towards the fountain, “because the Seven is underwater, it looks like it’s in a slightly different spot than it really is. The water is playing a trick on our eyes, bending the light like a funhouse mirror!” Bunny Bell tilted her head, her long ears perked up in curiosity. A trick? Whoa! A funhouse mirror in the water! That’s so silly and smart! Cog continued, his enthusiasm growing, “We need to use that trick! If we look at where the water makes it look like the Seven is, and then aim just below that spot, we might be able to grab the real Seven that’s hiding beneath the illusion!” It was a bit of a wobbly thought, but Cog’s ideas were usually very good ones.

Finally, the moment of truth arrived. Cog stood on the mossy edge of the fountain, his cool, smooth brass body gleaming in the afternoon sun, and Bunny Bell stood beside him, her little paws ready and twitching with anticipation. Cog looked carefully at the Seven through the rippling water. He squinted. “Okay, okay, okay,” he whispered, his voice a soft metallic hum. “It looks like it’s right there, a little bit higher than it actually is. The water is making it seem to float higher.” He pointed a precise, metallic finger. “So, we aim there, just a little bit lower than where it seems to be!” He then carefully lowered a long, thin brass grabber he’d ingeniously made from bent wire and a tiny spring. He aimed it at the spot Cog indicated, a spot that looked just a hair below the watery reflection of the Seven. He slowly, carefully, lowered it into the cool water. *Plink… plink…* the wire whispered through the water. The water rippled gently. Bunny Bell held her breath. The grabber nudged something solid with a soft thud. Then, with a gentle, sure *scoop*, it lifted. Slowly, carefully, up it came, dripping with sparkling fountain water, smelling faintly of moss and sunshine. And there it was! The shining, beautiful number Seven, looking even more magnificent than before, glistening like a newly discovered jewel.

“YESSSSS!” cheered Bunny Bell, her ears doing a wild, happy wiggle dance. Cog carefully brought the Seven closer, and Bunny Bell, with trembling paws full of pure delight, took the precious number. She looked up at Cog, her fluffy face beaming with gratitude. “Thank you, Cog! You’re the cleverest, most wonderful brass squirrel ever!” Cog gave a little brass bow, a perfect, precise movement. “It’s all about looking a little differently!” he whirred, his voice warm.

And that’s what Bunny Bell learned! She still loved collecting shiny things with all her heart, but she learned to be a little more patient, to take a deep breath and observe before she acted. And she and Cog the brass squirrel, the wobbly-water-wonder team, became the very best of treasure-hunting friends in town, always ready for the next sparkly adventure, together.
characters: Bunny Bell, Cog the brass squirrel
